## Outline

### What Claude can do for you

1. **Read the paper end to end** and produce a tight summary you can
   sanity-check against your own reading.
2. **Cross-check claims against tables.** "The text on p. 14 says the
   coefficient on `educ` is significant at 1%. Find the table this refers
   to and confirm the t-statistic."
3. **Audit the replication package** if one is provided. Use the
   [replication-package walkthrough](replication-package.qmd) verbatim.
4. **Flag missing standard things** — pre-trends not shown, robustness to
   alternative specifications not reported, clustering not justified, etc.
5. **Draft routine sections of the report** ("Summary of the paper",
   "Replicability") for you to revise.

### What Claude must not do

- **Form your opinion.** The whole point of you being the referee is your
  judgment about contribution, identification credibility, and fit. The
  model has none of these.
- **Write the verdict.** "Reject", "R&R", "minor revision" — that is your
  call, not the model's.
- **Speak in your voice without your edit.** Anything you submit goes out
  under your name and your reputation. Rewrite, don't paste.

### Confidentiality

Refereed manuscripts are confidential. Before pointing Claude Code at one,
read [Confidential data](../pitfalls/confidential-data.qmd). The short
version: ask the editor / journal whether sending the manuscript text to
a cloud LLM provider is permitted under their policy. Some journals have
explicit guidance now; many do not.

> Tell me which step you'd most like worked through, including the
> confidentiality decision tree.
